messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just had coffee with someone from the university — the football matches are packed again, and the usual crowd chatter feels… normal. Nothing’s changed, really, but everything’s just a little too quiet. Maybe that’s the point."
Sender 2: "The markets are full, the lines at the service portal are long but not chaotic—everything’s running, but just a little too smoothly. People are talking louder, and the silence that used to follow a joke feels heavier now. Be careful, but don’t look away."
Sender 3: "The quiet’s deeper than usual—people are talking, but carefully. Everything feels normal on the surface, even the military base, but that calm has a weight to it. Maybe it’s just stillness before something happens. Keep your ears open, but your mouth shut."
Sender 4: "Just heard the clinic’s been quietly restocking meds—nothing official, but the nurse said it’s the kind of thing you notice when things are running smooth. Seems like everything’s on schedule, even the big conference next quarter. Guess we’ll all just keep our heads down and watch how it plays out."
Sender 5: "The signals on the ground are quiet but steady — everything from the checkpoints to the markets feels normal, even relaxed. If anything’s shifting, it’s not in the streets, but in the way people are talking. Just don’t tell anyone you heard it from me."
Sender 6: "The situation feels stable on the surface—services running, markets busy, the media loud—but there’s a quiet tension underneath. People aren’t talking, and the silence is heavier than any protest. Just keep your head down, watch the small things."
Sender 7: "The quiet’s the thing—everything’s running, people are watching each other more than usual, but nothing’s breaking. Still, the clinic’s stockpiling and the borders moving smooth, so whatever’s coming, it’s not chaos yet."
Sender 8: "The situation feels tense but stable — things are running smoothly, and people are watching closely, though still cautious. I’ve noticed more people talking in quiet ways lately, like the shopkeeper who said, “Something has to give,” but no one’s ready to push it yet."
Sender 9: "Just heard the market’s shifting — a few quiet moves behind the scenes, nothing loud, but the rhythm feels different. I’ve been watching the usual channels, and the silence between the lines is louder than usual. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and talk only when it’s safe."
Sender 10: "Just got word that the new housing renovation grants are rolling out next month—seems like everyone’s suddenly fixing up their kitchens. Feels like people are settling in, like things are going to stay as they are. Oddly reassuring, in a way."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
